newsitem.title: USA: Protesters arrested after dangling from bridge.
newsitem.headline: Protesters arrested after dangling from bridge.

text.p: Eight Greenpeace activists were arrested on Monday after dangling 75 feet (22 metres) from a bridge for two days to stop factory trawlers from taking to sea and fishing off Alaska where the protesters said they would harm sea life.
Police took five women and three men into custody and said they will be charged with reckless endangerment of others. The charge carries a maximum fine of $5,000 and one year in prison.
Federal charges for blocking a commercially navigable waterway also were possible, police said.
"We feel it's been a tremendous success," said Dave Batker, a protest organizer. "We have blocked three factory trawlers from leaving. We feel that our message has really gone out."
The demonstration started on Saturday when the protesters tried to hang a 400-foot (133-metre) fishing net from the bridge to stop factory trawlers from passing underneath en route to Alaskan waters.
But the police intervened, enabling one trawler to pass through and leaving the protestors suspended from the Aurora bridge.

Greenpeace wants the big trawlers banned from Alaskan waters. The activists argue that such large ships, known as factory trawlers because they catch and process huge amounts of fish on board, take pollock in direct competition with marine mammals such as the Stellar sea lion, which was declared an endangered species in May.
But the American Factory Trawler Association denies that North Pacific fishing is endangering wildlife.
